scenes.say: Ever wonder why distributed systems can't guarantee everything at once? Let's crack the CAP theorem.

scenes.label: CAP
scenes.sub: Only two of Consistency, Availability, or Partition tolerance can be guaranteed at once.
scenes.say: CAP says you can only pick two out of consistency, availability, and partition tolerance. You can't have all three.
Eventual consistency means data might lag, but catches up. Strong consistency means every read is up to date.

scenes.question: Can a system guarantee all three CAP?
scenes.right: No, network partitions force a trade-off.
scenes.say: Don't fall for this classic trap. In a partition, you must choose: consistency or availability. You can't guarantee both.
